thread:
Rafael Mendes: Kicking off breaker threshold defaults discussion for Hosted. We need something sane for Phase 1 that doesn’t flap like crazy. I pulled last 30d signals from us-east + eu-west (hosted pool) and plotted queue depth + p99 + GPU util.

Quick chart (from Grafana panel):
- Normal: queue_depth ~ 50–300, GPU util 55–85%, p99 0.8–1.6s
- Mild overload: queue_depth 600–1200, GPU util 90–95%, p99 3–6s
- Bad events: queue_depth spikes 2000–5000, GPU util pinned 97–99%, p99 10–25s + timeouts

Question: what should be our open/close thresholds + cooldown? We want deterministic shedding before tail latency falls off a cliff.

Christine Wong: Thanks. First gut check: we should bias toward queue depth / scheduler wait time, not GPU util. Util has lag and gets weird with prefill-heavy bursts.

Christine Wong: Also: can we define separate thresholds per model class? e.g. “long-context” models hit memory pressure sooner. If we do one-size-fits-all, we’ll either shed too early or too late.

Tomáš Novák: +1 on util lag. During the Jan incident we saw GPU util at 88–92% while queues were exploding, because the runtime was thrashing KV and not doing useful work.

Aisha Bello: For flapping: we need (a) hysteresis and (b) minimum-open duration.

Aisha Bello: Something like:
- open when signal > open_threshold for 30s (or N consecutive samples)
- stay open for at least 90s
- half-open probe window 30s
- close only if signal < close_threshold for 2–3 minutes

Sergio Costa: What’s our sample interval on these metrics right now? Some are 10s, some 30s.

Caleb Johnson: Gateway admission decisions are 10s rollup; routing capacity snapshots are 15s; runtime queue depth is 10s. We can standardize evaluation window to 30s/60s inside the breaker service, but make sure we’re not doing per-request evaluation from raw metrics.

Peter Holtz: I’d propose the initial breaker input set is very small:
1) queue_depth (runtime bounded queue)
2) scheduler_wait_ms p95
3) memory_pressure flag (KV cache / OOM proximity)

Peter Holtz: If any hard guardrail trips (memory_pressure), open immediately with a longer cooldown.

Sean Gallagher: Whatever we pick, the big failure mode is breaker flapping -> clients retry -> we amplify load. So defaults must be conservative and stable.

Sean Gallagher: We should also align with error semantics: if we shed, it must be 429/503 with Retry-After. No silent timeouts.

Rafael Mendes: Agree. For Phase 1, we can keep “routing breaker” simple and still rely on gateway early shed once breaker is open.

Rafael Mendes: Draft thresholds (very rough):
- open if queue_depth > 2000 for 30s OR scheduler_wait_p95 > 1500ms for 30s
- close if queue_depth < 800 for 180s AND scheduler_wait_p95 < 600ms for 180s
- cooldown: 120s

Thoughts?

Christine Wong: 2000 feels high if we’re trying to prevent p99 collapse. In your chart, once we cross ~1200 we’re already at 3–6s p99.

Christine Wong: Suggest open closer to 1200–1500 for 30s, but only for non-streaming? Streaming has different failure characteristics (disconnects are more visible).

Elena Popov: From routing POV, I’d rather open earlier and route to fallback if possible. If we open at 2000, there’s often no capacity left to do graceful degradation.

Benji Okafor: Reminder: config schema supports per (region, model_class, tier) override, but we need safe defaults. We can ship:
- default_open_queue_depth
- default_close_queue_depth
- min_open_seconds
- half_open_max_rps (or token budget)

Benji Okafor: I can enforce close < open via validation.

Sergio Costa: Re: charts, can you paste the actual panels? Want to sanity check what “queue depth 1200” means: is it incoming requests waiting, or internal batches?

Rafael Mendes: It’s runtime inbound request queue depth (pre-scheduler). Not batch queue. Panel link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/overload-hosted/queue?var-region=us-east (internal)

Rafael Mendes: Screenshot summary (for folks not in Grafana):
- At ~1000 queue depth, scheduler wait p95 ~700–1100ms
- At ~1500 queue depth, scheduler wait p95 ~1.4–2.2s
- Above 2000, scheduler wait p95 > 3s and p99 latency blows out.

Aisha Bello: If we want to stop the p99 blowout, open should trigger around when scheduler_wait_p95 crosses ~1.5s. That’s more portable than queue depth.

Aisha Bello: Queue depth is still useful, but it scales with request type (long prompt vs short).

Tomáš Novák: Strongly prefer scheduler wait as primary. Queue depth can be gamed by batching changes.

Christine Wong: Proposed rule (v1):
- open when scheduler_wait_p95 > 1500ms for 60s
- also open if queue_depth > 1500 for 60s
- close when scheduler_wait_p95 < 700ms for 180s AND queue_depth < 800 for 180s
- min open 120s

Christine Wong: That gives us a wider band and avoids jitter around 1500.

Sean Gallagher: +1, but we need to be careful about “for 60s” vs “for 30s”. If we wait too long, the system tips and takes minutes to recover.

Peter Holtz: We can do 30s for open but require 6 consecutive samples @ 5s or 10s? That gives us faster response without opening on a single spike.

Caleb Johnson: We don’t have 5s consistent sampling everywhere. But we can do “N out of M” evaluation internally. e.g. 3 out of last 4 samples over threshold.

Allison Grant: One more flapping issue: if we use too many labels (model, region, tier, route) we’ll have lots of small breakers with noisy signals.

Allison Grant: For defaults I’d suggest breaker granularity = (model, region, tier) only. Don’t add customer_id or route in Phase 1.

Rafael Mendes: Yes, keep cardinality sane. Also consistent with ADR direction.

Sergio Costa: Another thought: incorporate “shed_rate” as a feedback signal to avoid oscillation. If we’re already shedding 20% and queue still rising, keep open longer.

Aisha Bello: That becomes a control loop; risky for Phase 1. But we can extend cooldown when memory_pressure is the trigger.

Elena Popov: +1. Keep it deterministic. If memory pressure trips, open immediately, cooldown 5 minutes, and only half-open slowly.

Benji Okafor: Can we formalize reason-specific cooldowns in config?
- OPEN_REASON=queue_wait: cooldown 120s
- OPEN_REASON=mem_pressure: cooldown 300s

I can add it as `cooldown_seconds_by_reason`.

Christine Wong: Works for me, but we should cap complexity. Maybe only two buckets: “soft overload” and “hard overload”.

Tomáš Novák: On retry storms: do we have a stance on Retry-After values? If we open for 120s but tell clients Retry-After: 1, they’ll hammer us.

Sean Gallagher: Good catch. We should align Retry-After with breaker state. If breaker open, Retry-After should reflect a fraction of cooldown (e.g., 5–15s with jitter) not 1s.

Rafael Mendes: I’d like to pick:
- gateway returns `Retry-After: 10` while breaker open
- SDK guidance: exponential backoff with jitter, respect Retry-After

Christine Wong: 10s is reasonable. But if we’re half-open probing, we should still return Retry-After on rejections.

Allison Grant: Observability note: we need a panel showing breaker transitions vs scheduler_wait_p95 and queue_depth. Otherwise we’ll never debug “why did it open?”

Sergio Costa: I can add:
- timeseries: `breaker_state{state=open}` as a stepped line
- annotate transitions open/half-open/closed
- overlay `scheduler_wait_p95_ms` and `queue_depth`

Sergio Costa: Also a heatmap for `open_reason` counts.

Caleb Johnson: Please make sure `open_reason` label is bounded. Don’t put raw strings from runtime.

Rafael Mendes: Action items:
1) Christine + Peter: propose final default thresholds for soft/hard overload (include windows + hysteresis)
2) Benji: confirm schema supports reason-specific cooldown and validation (close < open)
3) Sergio + Allison: add dashboard panels for breaker transitions and confirm label cardinality constraints
4) Rafael: write up in working notes doc + post to #eng-platform for review

Rafael Mendes: Tentative default (to converge):
SOFT overload breaker:
- open if scheduler_wait_p95 > 1500ms for 30s OR queue_depth > 1500 for 30s
- min open 120s
- half-open after cooldown 120s, allow 5% of normal admission
- close if scheduler_wait_p95 < 700ms for 180s AND queue_depth < 800 for 180s
HARD overload breaker (mem pressure):
- open immediately on memory_pressure=true
- cooldown 300s
- close only after memory_pressure=false for 180s AND scheduler_wait_p95 < 700ms

React with :thumbsup: if you can live with this as Phase 1 default.

Christine Wong: :thumbsup: with one tweak: consider open if scheduler_wait_p95 > 1200ms for 30s for long-context model class.

Tomáš Novák: :thumbsup: +1 to model-class override, otherwise this is fine to ship behind flag.

Aisha Bello: :thumbsup: looks good. I’ll add note: alerting should not page on shed errors; page on internal 5xx + control plane latency.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: and I’ll document label restrictions + required metrics.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: Ship it behind flag. Let’s make sure we can adjust these without redeploy and have a quick rollback.

Rafael Mendes: Cool. I’ll post a summary + links in the working notes doc and tag Mina/Ravi for routing review.

Logan Wright: Late to thread — +1. If we’re standardizing on scheduler_wait_p95, we should confirm it’s emitted for all runtime versions in hosted. I’ll verify telemetry coverage today and report back.
